title: Live trade review: amend_position_sl.py --mandate/--evidence, provenance live_review_mandate, min_buffer_atr + once-per-bar bounds in code, evidence-on-main check, apply_mode switch
note: From docs/plans/live-trade-review-DESIGN.md § 8 (merged c5d8d225, operator-approved 2026-10-25 ~13:58Z). Parent LIVE-TRADE-REVIEW-DESIGN. Design § 4. Tier 2 (order path): landing hold, manager merge on data. [2026-10-25 LTR-3-SKILL, session_01R3JNyuLvWTXNqU8HKspiHP] FINDING (operator structural directive ~16:15Z: the review is package-level; each account applies an intent ONLY through its own risk layer/executor, within its own bounds, DD limits and prop rules, so each prop account can decide for itself). The design section 4 apply path does NOT do that. scripts/ops/amend_position_sl.py moves the shared order_packages.sl and every leg's stop (live + mirror + soak) in one pass, and it calls no RiskManager. RiskManager.approve() (src/units/accounts/risk.py, def approve -> evaluate) is only reached for NEW order packages. So an open-trade amend today bypasses per-account risk entirely, and a prop account cannot refuse a package-level tighten on its own rules. LTR-6 (Bybit), LTR-8 (prop) and LTR-9 (Alpaca) each need a per-account apply hook: the account's risk layer evaluates an amend intent (tighten-only, min_buffer_atr, daily-loss/DD distance) and returns apply or refuse with a reason, and the result is written back to the review row's account_reads. NOT built by LTR-3. The skill records account_reads read-only and labels a Bybit would_apply as 'the shared amend would reach this leg', not 'the account's risk layer approved it'.
